2
Read with an adult
Ask an adult to read the words and help you find a page. Take turns. Ask
questions. Everyone can join in.
Use your textbook
Keep this textbook for reading and sharing. Say, point or use objects. Write
and draw in your workbook or an ordinary exercise book.
Find a lesson
Look at the contents on the next pages. The number beside a title tells you
the page in THIS textbook. An adult can help you read the page numbers.
Try in your own way
You can speak, point, move objects or draw. Use safe materials within easy
reach. Take time to explain your thinking.

Adult support and sources
Maths with Friends  •  Textbook
9
Shared introductions
Textbook annual 10–12 = Opening textbook source 2–4. Children are introduced on 10–11;
teachers on 12.
Using older page references
Copied lesson pages name their source in the top strip. A textbook/workbook page reference
inside a copied lesson means that local source page, not the annual page. Convert it using
pages 6–8. P1-01 and P1-02 share the Opening source; later chapters use their own named
source extracts.
Complete answers and teaching guidance
Textbook annual 273: annual adult guide. Annual 274–283: new questions with complete
answers and exact question pages in both books. Annual 284: fresh and delayed rechecks.
Annual 286–406: chapter guidance, complete original answers, misconceptions, help and
rechecks; use pages 6–8 to find each chapter.
Words, sources, credits and next year
Textbook annual 285: annual glossary, sources, credits and Primary 2 preview. Original chapter
word lists, curriculum mappings, sources and credits remain in textbook annual 286–406. These
adult pages are shared support for both books.
Edition and artwork
English-only, full-colour A4 annual pair. Cover: existing selected textbook v4 / workbook v2
illustrations, credited in artwork/covers/primary-1-provenance.json. Teaching artwork and
deterministic counting diagrams retain their source credits. Cover art is decorative; do not use
its objects for counting tasks.
Evidence and approval limits
Provisional historical baseline with documented additions. Suggested terms are editorial
estimates. Current NERDC/Gombe alignment or adoption, local educator review, pupil and
accessibility trials, physical print tests and printer approval remain pending. Independent
editorial review is separate; this export is not press-ready.

MATHS WITH FRIENDS
PRIMARY ONE / TEXTBOOK
MEET OUR LEARNING CLUB
Meet your friends
An adult can read with you. There is a place for you too.
Read together. Keep this textbook reusable.
Aishatu
The box-toy builder
I'm Aishatu from Gombe. My cousins and I
make toy shops from old boxes.
I like building things and trying new ideas.
I don't like long waits. Let's make something!
Adamu
The game storyteller
I'm Adamu. My family is from Dukku. My
cousins turn my funny stories into games.
I like stories and fair turns.
I don't like anyone being left out. Come and
play!
What do you like to make or play?
MATHS WITH FRIENDS / TEXTBOOK

MATHS WITH FRIENDS
PRIMARY ONE / TEXTBOOK
MEET OUR LEARNING CLUB
More friends to meet
An adult can read with you. There is a place for you too.
Read together. Keep this textbook reusable.
Grace
The notebook explorer
I'm Grace. My family is from Billiri.
Grandfather and I keep a discovery notebook.
I like neat drawings and tiny details.
I don't like smudges. But I can try again!
John
The puzzle-map maker
I'm John. My family is from Yamaltu/Deba. I
make puzzle maps for my cousins.
I use a wheelchair. I like drawing secret paths.
I don't like answers before I've had a try!
You belong here too. Let us learn and help one another.
MATHS WITH FRIENDS / TEXTBOOK

MATHS WITH FRIENDS
PRIMARY ONE / TEXTBOOK
OUR TWO TEACHERS
Meet your teachers
Two friendly guides for our learning club.
Read together. Keep this textbook reusable.
Mrs Binta
Big ideas. Brave little tries.
Hello! I'm Mrs Binta. I turn everyday things
into maths games. I like curious questions
and brave tries. In my class, a mistake is a
chance to learn. Bring your ideas!
Mr Aliyu
Riddles, games and discoveries.
Hello! I'm Mr Aliyu. I enjoy number riddles
and building games. I like asking, 'How did
you know?' We will sort and match together.
I can't wait to hear your ideas!
You can ask questions, try an idea and have another go.

CHAPTER ONE / ONE TO FIVE
A cup for every friend
We will count, read, write and order one to five.
Read together. Keep this textbook reusable.
Touch one.
Say one number.
Mrs Binta: After play, Aishatu brings cups for her friends. Every friend needs
a cup.
Aishatu: I cannot wait!
Adamu: Can everyone have a fair turn?
Grace: I will help check our cup record.
John: Let me try the counting puzzle first.
Mrs Binta leads our counting lesson.
Use large unbreakable cups at a reachable table.

one
two
three

Grace: We can check again.

number word. Then say how many.
Do this with real cups too. Move each counted cup aside.

1 2 3 4 5
John: I want to try before a hint.

Adamu: I touched a cup twice. How can I check?
Tell or show a partner how to count each cup just once.

Grace: Each friend has a cup.

John: We solved the puzzle.

A fresh try. Work on your own.
Ask an adult to name a number from one to five.
Make that many cups or counters at the table.
Ask the adult to mix numeral cards from one to five.
Point to the numeral the adult says.
Now the adult points to a mixed card. Say its number.

Read together. Keep this textbook reusable.
Sort.
Match.
Put in order.
Mr Aliyu: Let us prepare a classroom game. First, sort the leaves and bottle tops.
Aishatu: I brought a box for our game pieces.
Grace: I like things in their places.
Adamu: Let us take fair turns.
John: Can we find out which set has more?
Mr Aliyu: These are our game pieces. Watch me sort them. Then we can check: are
there more bottle tops or leaves?

bottle tops.
Leaves together
Bottle tops together
Grace: I put a leaf with the bottle tops by mistake.
Mr Aliyu: Check our rule. Where should it go?
Grace: With the leaves. I can try again.
Try together. I circled one leaf. Point to the other leaf. Then point to

Mr Aliyu: I draw a line from one bottle top to one bottle top. Each bottle

Two bottle tops in the lower set have no partner.
Four is more than two. Two is fewer than four.
I circle the whole set with more.
Adamu: The long row must have more!
Mr Aliyu: Let us match and check.
Use your finger to match each bottle top in the upper row to a different bottle

2
3
4
Aishatu: I want to rush to the game.
Mr Aliyu: Pause and count each set first.
In your exercise book, write these numbers from smallest to

In your exercise book, draw a set of 1 dot.
Beside it, draw a separate set of 3 dots.

Need a smaller step? Point from each upper dot to a different lower

Finish matching with your finger. Point to the set with more.

Adamu: Your turn, then mine!

John: Point to the set with more.

Grace: The two spare bottle tops are away. Now the tray is tidy.

Is the game mat empty?

Look inside.
Is it empty?

nine

the same way up. Do not turn a 6 over to make a 9.
6
Start near the top. Curve down and around.
Close the loop at the bottom.
7
Start at the top left. Draw across to the right.
Slant down to the left.
8
Start near the top. Make a small loop,
then a lower loop. Join them neatly.
9
Make the loop at the top first.
Then draw the downstroke on the right.

opposite sides; non-square rectangle has unequal adjacent sides. Circle:

Prepare a reachable table, large smooth paper strips, safe removable head-marking
materials and full-size upright paper silhouettes with clear head tops and foot
baseline. Adult positions paper on a reachable surface; no stools, climbing, sharp pins
or touching pupils. Printed figures are small method diagrams, never life-size. A
seated pupil can mark stand-ins with positioning help. Do not require John or anyone
to stand; never compare sitting height with standing stature.
Use a consenting adult to role-play two different fictional people for each collection.
One can play a home role and another a school role. Choose new completed-year
ages within taught number range; reply only AFTER the child asks. Never present a
completed table as interviewing evidence. Real collection is private and voluntary:
accept decline, substitute fictional roles, do not display identifiable ages; letters alone
do not guarantee privacy.
Score separately: permission/consistent question; listening and accurate age
recording; labelled new head marks/common baseline; comparison and accurate
recording. Record fictional simulated versus actual willing-person collection, resource
positioning/reading/transcription help versus mathematical prompts. Accept all
accurate conditional ages and taller/shorter/equal results. No resources: practical
collection not assessed. Do not invent success. Copies of printed records assess
interpretation only.
Misconceptions: next birthday equals completed age; letter equals age; taller means better; misaligned
strips compare fairly. Concrete help: interview one role, read back; mark one strip then another, align
bottoms, compare. Recall before help; new unsupported recheck; new fresh and scheduled delayed
collection. Local educator, pupil/accessibility trials, print and printer approval remain pending.
